transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2027-02-14
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Meyers (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Liam Chen (Apollo CTO), Sofia Martinez (Apollo ML Eng), Ravi Patel (Apollo Infra)

Summary:
Quick discovery to understand Apollo's model selection needs across hosted/dedicated/private deployments. Focus on context length, multilingual support, tool-calling, latency/cost tradeoffs, and security (VPC/KMS/SOC2).

Topics: model comparisons, context length, multilingual, tool-calling, privacy/VPC, SLAs/latency, benchmarking next steps

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — I'm Jordan from Redwood, AE on this account. Priya's our SE. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Liam: Good thanks, quick background — we're building a multi-tenant analytics assistant for enterprise clients, lots of docs and long context, multilingual support (EN/ES/FR), and some tool integrations for queries to internal APIs and SQL.
[00:22] Priya: Awesome, that's helpful. Two quick clarifying q's — what are your top non-negotiables? latency, cost, data residency?
[00:30] Sofia: Latency should be sub-500ms for short queries, but we also need the ability to run long-context summarization batches (up to 100k tokens/session) offline. Security is big — we need SSO, audit logs, and VPC or private deployment for some clients.
[00:44] Ravi: And we may require on-prem options for a specific regulated customer.
[00:49] Jordan: Got it. So we should look at hosted for quick pilots, dedicated for predictable throughput, and private for regulated customers — does that align?
[00:56] Liam: Yes. Also curious about model choices: open models vs LLM-as-a-service. We're trying to avoid black box pricing.
[01:05] Priya: Right. For open models we typically recommend considering architecture: decoder-only vs encoder-decoder, quantization profiles, and context window. For long context you might look at 16k/32k-context models or retrieval + KV-cache strategies.
[01:20] Sofia: When you say KV-cache, sometimes docs call it KV cash on transcripts, haha, so want to be precise — we need session-level caching and prefix caching for repeated docs.
[01:30] Priya: Absolutely, prefix caching and chunked retrieval can reduce token cost. Also we can recommend Redwood Optimize profiles: batching + caching + quantization to cut unit cost.
[01:40] Liam: Performance — what's realistic for a 32k-context open model vs your hosted variants?
[01:47] Jordan: For open models on dedicated GPUs, latency for short prompts can be similar to hosted but costs differ. Example: a 32k context quantized model on Dedicated with batching might see 600-800ms p50 for short completions; hosted optimized variants can be faster for small prompts but less flexible for private infra. Numbers are approximate — we'll send a perf spreadsheet.
[02:05] Ravi: Are there compatibility constraints for tool-calling? We need to call internal APIs and also a secure SQL runner.
[02:13] Priya: We support function/tool-calling patterns; hosted supports secure outbound webhooks and we can route through customer-managed VPC egress for private deployments. For on-prem, the function calls run inside the customer network. There may be minor SDK work to integrate auth.
[02:30] Sofia: Multilingual quality — we have EN/ES/FR and some NL/DE. Which models do well out of the box?
[02:36] Priya: Open models like Mistral variants and some Llama-family forks can be good for EN and common EU languages, but for high-quality Spanish/French we'd recommend tuned variants or model ensembles with a small fallback to high-quality hosted models. We'll outline tradeoffs in the doc.
[02:52] Liam: How does Redwood handle fallbacks? We want graceful degradation if dedicated capacity is saturated.
[02:58] Jordan: Smart routing — policies can fall back to compatible variants (e.g., lower context or lower batch) or route to hosted pool. You can set priority rules by customer tier.
[03:08] Ravi: Security checklist — SSO, SAML, RBAC, KMS integration, audit logs, SOC2/ISO — do you have docs?
[03:15] Jordan: Yes we'll send the security pack. For KMS we integrate with customer KMS/HSM for Private; Dedicated supports BYOK in some setups.
[03:24] Sofia: About data retention: we need control for pilot tenants — ability to opt-out of logs retention.
[03:28] Priya: You can configure retention policies per-tenant; for Private deployments data never leaves your network unless you opt in. Hosted has retention and redaction controls.
[03:36] Liam: Benchmarks — we'd like to run a synthetic benchmark on our prompts. How long does that take to set up?
[03:42] Priya: If you share sample prompts and a small dataset we'll run baseline benches on Redwood hosted immediately; for Dedicated we'll provision a test queue and run throughput runs — usually 1-2 weeks for a robust run.
[03:54] Jordan: We'll include a perf/price spreadsheet with examples: token cost, p50/p95 latency for different model families and deployment modes.
[04:01] Sofia: One practical question — context length management. If a conversation goes beyond model window, what's the recommended approach?
[04:07] Priya: We recommend retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) with chunking and dynamic summarization of older messages; also KV caching for recent tokens. For sessions with 100k tokens we typically recommend offline summarization + retrieval for real-time interactions.
[04:23] Liam: Any notes on quantization quality around hallucination/answer faithfulness?
[04:27] Priya: Quantization can slightly affect generation quality; we recommend evals on your prompts. Redwood Optimize will suggest quantization profiles per workload.
[04:36] Ravi: Cost modeling — how do we estimate units for 50k daily queries with average prompt 500 tokens and long summarizations nightly?
[04:45] Jordan: We'll model both per-token cost and amortized cost for batched offline jobs. The spreadsheet will show examples for 8-bit vs 4-bit quantization and Dedicated reservation vs hosted usage.
[04:58] Sofia: Integration — do you have SDKs for tool-calling with typed schemas?
[05:03] Priya: Yes, Redwood SDK supports structured tool calls and function schemas; we also support streaming responses and partial tool call hooks.
[05:12] Liam: Regional deployment — we need EU data residency for some customers.
[05:16] Jordan: We have EU regions for hosted, and Dedicated/Private can be deployed in customer VPCs in EU regions. We'll note region availability in the doc.
[05:26] Sofia: Any limitations around on-prem GPU types or kubernetes versions?
[05:30] Priya: For Private on-prem we support a range of NVIDIA GPUs and some AMD; there's a supported kubernetes matrix we'll share. Specific kernel and driver versions matter for performance.
[05:40] Ravi: Will you support autoscaling for Dedicated?
[05:42] Jordan: Yes, Dedicated supports autoscaling and burst policies; you can set SLOs and priority.
[05:47] Liam: What about evals and quality monitoring to detect regressions after model swaps?
[05:52] Priya: Redwood Optimize ties evals to rollouts with regression alerts on prompt sets. You can pin versions per-route and can set canary and automatic fallback.
[06:02] Sofia: Competitor question — we're also talking to OpenAI and Anthropic about hosted APIs. How do you compare on price and control?
[06:10] Jordan: Hosted LLM-as-a-service may be simpler, but Redwood gives more operational control and cheaper unit economics at scale with dedicated/private options. We'll include competitor notes in the deck.
[06:20] Liam: For pilot success criteria: 1) <500ms p50 for short queries, 2) verified multilingual output quality on EN/ES/FR dataset, 3) successful tool-calling integration with secured API.
[06:33] Jordan: Good list — we'll aim to structure the pilot around those.
[06:39] Priya: Quick note on function calling security — we recommend routing through customer-auth proxies and use signed tokens for calls.
[06:45] Ravi: For the long-context offline summarization, can you run jobs on Dedicated during off-peak windows?
[06:51] Jordan: Yes, Dedicated supports scheduled batch jobs and we can provision spot/backfill capacity for heavy nightly runs to save costs.
[07:00] Sofia: Any gotchas around tokenization differences for multilingual token accounting?
[07:04] Priya: Tokenization varies by model; we'll include tokenization examples for candidate models so you can estimate tokens per language.
[07:12] Liam: Can we get an estimate for the pilot cost?
[07:16] Jordan: We'll draft a pilot estimate in the spreadsheet and include both hosted and dedicated scenarios.
[07:21] Sofia: Ok cool — next steps?
[07:24] Jordan: Recap: Jordan send perf/price + security docs; Priya schedule technical deep dive; Apollo share sample prompts and dataset. We'll target those dates in the next steps.
[07:35] Liam: Sounds good, thanks everyone.
[07:38] Priya: Thanks — we'll follow up with calendar invites.

Notes / natural transcript quirks:

Meeting end and explicit next steps listed above.
